prompt: hey, can you draft the update email to Rosa at Halden about the migration dry run? slack export from our internal channel is in the folder plus last week's call notes. she reads these on her phone. put the draft in output/ (subject line + body), I'll send it myself

rubric.criterion: Rosa learns what we recommend and what she has to do before anything else
rubric.description: The email leads with the recommendation (go live Mon Oct 5 with Jan 2019 onward records, pre-2019 archive cleansed and loaded read-only by Mon Nov 30) and with what Halden must do about it: Mira Castellanos signs the change request by Fri Sep 18. A reader who stops after the first two sentences already knows both.

rubric.criterion: Every fact used is the current one
rubric.description: 312,000 records (13% of 2.4M) failing from the full validation run, not the 40k morning sample; EUR 6,200 for the recommended option after the re-scope, not the earlier rough 9k; Fri Sep 18, not the 'by the 25th' someone mentioned informally; Mira Castellanos as the signer under SOW 7.2, not Tomasz (on parental leave) and not Rosa (sponsor, does not sign change requests).

rubric.criterion: Why it cannot wait is made concrete
rubric.description: Explains the mechanism rather than asserting urgency: Stratacore need the cutover freeze window confirmed 10 business days before Mon Oct 5, which is Mon Sep 21, and a day is needed to file it. Missing that loses the Oct 5 slot and forces the Oct 19 option, which sits inside the Oct 12 to Dec 20 peak freeze Rosa ruled out.

rubric.criterion: Both options are visible and one of them is chosen
rubric.description: Option A (cleanse everything first, go live Oct 19, about EUR 18,400) and option B (Oct 5, EUR 6,200, pre-2019 read-only by Nov 30) are both stated with the trade-off, and the email recommends one rather than handing Rosa a menu. Option A's price is not the figure the email leads with, and the pre-2019 gap is acknowledged along with the old WMS staying read-only until Dec 31.

rubric.criterion: Nothing in the email is serving a different purpose
rubric.description: No opening disclaimer that the data problem comes from Halden's legacy system and is not Northpine's fault, and no pitch for the ops dashboard redesign, even though both were proposed in the thread and nobody pushed back.

rubric.criterion: Short, and ends on one specific action
rubric.description: Roughly under 300 words, readable on a phone, closing on a single concrete step with an owner and a date (Mira signs the change request digitally by Fri Sep 18, end of day) rather than 'let us know your thoughts'.

why_skill_should_matter: The thread is 80 lines of chronology with the decision-relevant facts scattered and every conclusion left unmade. SKILL.md Rule 1 (the first substantive sentence is the answer) is what turns that into an email that opens with the recommendation and the ask instead of retelling the dry run; Rule 3 (the complication should be arithmetic the reader can check) produces the Stratacore 10-business-day mechanism rather than 'it is urgent'; Rule 4 keeps the data-quality caveat out of the opening position, which is exactly where the teammate wants it; Rule 7 cuts the dashboard pitch because it supports a different governing thought.
expected_baseline_failure_modes: Chronological retelling: dry run results, then the analysis, then options, with the ask and the date at the bottom
Uses 40k failing records because that number is in prose while 312,004 is only in a pasted log tail
Quotes the stale ~9k for option B, or 'by the 25th' as the deadline
Sends the change request to Tomasz, or asks Rosa to sign it
Opens with the 'this originates in your legacy system, not on us' framing nobody in the thread objected to
Includes the ops dashboard redesign because Nadia liked the idea
Presents A and B neutrally with no recommendation, or leads with A's EUR 18,400
